lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Digital Life, Purchases, and Consumer Skills
lessonRef.title: Correction and reflection: digital cleanup

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic digital cleanup task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner reviews the apps or files on a device they are allowed to manage, or a shared device with permission from whoever manages it, and sorts a real set of items into keep, remove, or archive based on how recently and often each is actually used.
safetyNotes: The learner only manages devices or accounts they are allowed to change, and asks first before deleting anything on a shared device.
When unsure whether an item might still be needed, move it to a trash, recycle, or archive location instead of deleting it permanently, so it can still be recovered.

simulationAlternative.description: If the learner has no device they are allowed to manage, they instead sort a provided sample device-storage list of apps and files into keep, remove, or archive, explaining the reason for each decision.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific habit you will use to prevent this same buildup of unused items in the future, and why checking actual use is more reliable than judging by how useful something sounds.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Sorting accuracy and evidence: At least eight items are sorted into keep, remove, or archive based on actual last-used information. | Pattern analysis: A correct percentage is calculated and a specific pattern is named with at least one example. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner repeat this sort on a second device or account, with permission if it is shared, and compare which device accumulated more unused items and why.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic digital cleanup task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: digital cleanup worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner reviews the apps or files on a device they are allowed to manage, or a shared device with permission from whoever manages it, and sorts a real set of items into keep, remove, or archive based on how recently and often each is actually used.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact digital cleanup decision or action.
Model move 2: List at least eight apps or files on a device you are allowed to manage, or a shared device with permission.
Model move 3: For each item, note the last time you actually used it and sort it into keep, remove, or archive based on that actual use, not on how useful it sounds.

Model check: Sorting accuracy and evidence: At least eight items are sorted into keep, remove, or archive based on actual last-used information. | Pattern analysis: A correct percentage is calculated and a specific pattern is named with at least one example.

resources.title: digital cleanup action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for digital cleanup.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: digital cleanup coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner reviews the apps or files on a device they are allowed to manage, or a shared device with permission from whoever manages it, and sorts a real set of items into keep, remove, or archive based on how recently and often each is actually used.
Coach direction: List at least eight apps or files on a device you are allowed to manage, or a shared device with permission.
Learner prompt: Name the device and list the eight or more items.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: digital cleanup complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: For each item, note the last time you actually used it and sort it into keep, remove, or archive based on that actual use, not on how useful it sounds.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I sorted at least eight items into keep, remove, or archive based on actual last use.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I asked permission before removing anything on a shared device.

Equal-access rule: If the learner has no device they are allowed to manage, they instead sort a provided sample device-storage list of apps and files into keep, remove, or archive, explaining the reason for each decision.

resources.title: digital cleanup minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Explain one specific habit you will use to prevent this same buildup of unused items in the future, and why checking actual use is more reliable than judging by how useful something sounds.

Success checks: Sorting accuracy and evidence: At least eight items are sorted into keep, remove, or archive based on actual last-used information. | Pattern analysis: A correct percentage is calculated and a specific pattern is named with at least one example.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: digital cleanup supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional digital cleanup condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Sorting accuracy and evidence: At least eight items are sorted into keep, remove, or archive based on actual last-used information. | Pattern analysis: A correct percentage is calculated and a specific pattern is named with at least one example..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner reviews the apps or files on a device they are allowed to manage, or a shared device with permission from whoever manages it, and sorts a real set of items into keep, remove, or archive based on how recently and often each is actually used.

Point to one model step only.

realRoute.title: digital cleanup — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
For each item, note the last time you actually used it and sort it into keep, remove, or archive based on that actual use, not on how useful it sounds.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: digital cleanup — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If the learner has no device they are allowed to manage, they instead sort a provided sample device-storage list of apps and files into keep, remove, or archive, explaining the reason for each decision.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain one specific habit you will use to prevent this same buildup of unused items in the future, and why checking actual use is more reliable than judging by how useful something sounds.
observableCriteria: Sorting accuracy and evidence: At least eight items are sorted into keep, remove, or archive based on actual last-used information.
Pattern analysis: A correct percentage is calculated and a specific pattern is named with at least one example.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Sorting accuracy and evidence: At least eight items are sorted into keep, remove, or archive based on actual last-used information. | Pattern analysis: A correct percentage is calculated and a specific pattern is named with at least one example.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l06-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
